subject: Suncrest renewal — commit elevation & onboarding burst
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@suncrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Suncrest renewal conversation and commit options

Hi Aisha —

Congrats on a strong rollout this quarter. As we start the renewal conversation for Suncrest.ai I wanted to outline a straightforward path to reduce unit cost while guaranteeing capacity for your peak campaigns. Current snapshot: you’re averaging ~3M generation tokens / month with occasional spikes up to ~6.5M. We recommend a stepped commit that balances cost and burstability:

- Option A (recommended): 5,000,000 tokens/month commit at a 12% unit discount vs current hosted rate; 20% burst pocket for onboarding months 1–3.
- Option B: 7,500,000 tokens/month commit at 18% discount and 10% sustained burst.

Key operational notes: dedicated soft-throttle thresholds (per-minute rate caps) to protect latency SLOs, and an automatic fallback to a quantized model variant if capacity-constrained. I’ve attached a proposal with rate examples and an estimated monthly bill comparison (Suncrest_Monthly_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf).

If procurement needs a clear overage/on-demand rate we propose $0.00035 per token above commit for Option A.

Can we book 30 minutes Friday to review live with your procurement and engineering? Marissa (cc’d) will help with onboarding ops and credits.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: Suncrest_Monthly_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@suncrest.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Suncrest Procurement <procurement@suncrest.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suncrest renewal conversation and commit options

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clearly laid out options. A few quick notes from my side after an internal sync:

- Finance is pushing for predictable spend and would prefer the 5M commit if we can keep the initial outlay modest.
- Procurement will need an explicit definition for the "burst pocket" and what happens once it's consumed. Also need confirmation on whether burst usage counts toward the next month or is billed separately.
- Our security team asked whether the fallback quantized variant changes our data residency or audit log footprint.

Looping in procurement; procurement team, can you share your standard contract checklist so Ben/Marissa can prep a redline-ready amendment?

I can do a 30-minute call Friday at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Aisha Turner
Head of Product, Suncrest.ai
aisha.turner@suncrest.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@suncrest.ai>, Suncrest Procurement <procurement@suncrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suncrest renewal conversation and commit options

Aisha / Procurement —

Thanks — answers inline below (and I’m looping Karthik for the latency/ops/quantization detail):

- Burst pocket mechanics: for Option A the 20% burst is an emergency buffer tied to the monthly commit (so 1st month example: commit 5,000,000 tokens + 1,000,000 burst). Burst consumption is billed at the committed unit price up to the burst amount; any usage beyond commit+burst is billed at the overage rate ($0.00035/token). Burst does not roll over — it is a per-month buffer.
- Onboarding credit: we can front-load a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 10% of Month 1 invoice to smooth cashflow.
- Quantized fallback: Karthik — can you confirm that the fallback keeps logs/telemetry intact and does not change region-specific data storage?

Karthik Iyer (SE): the quantized variant keeps the same API surface and logs remain in the same region/tenant. There is no change to audit logs — only a slightly different model binary. Latency delta is small (~10–20ms median) but reduces GPU utilization by ~18% on our benchmarks.

Next steps proposal:
1) We prepare a short amendment reflecting Option A (5M commit, 20% burst for months 1–3, onboarding credit applied month 1).
2) Procurement shares redline checklist by EOD Wed.
3) Final sign-off + DocuSign link sent by next Tue to align with finance cycle.

Attachment: Suncrest_Monthly_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)

-ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Turner <aisha.turner@suncrest.ai>, Suncrest Procurement <procurement@suncrest.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Suncrest amendment ready for signature — 5M commit (12mo)

Hi Aisha / Procurement —

Thanks for the productive call last week. Per our alignment this thread captures the final terms we will put into the amendment:

- Term: 12 months, effective 2026-10-01 through 2027-09-30.
- Monthly committed tokens: 5,000,000.
- Unit pricing: committed rate per token (as in v2 proposal).
- Burst: 20% monthly burst allowance for months 1–3 (applied against commit, billed at commit unit price).
- Overage: $0.00035/token above commit+burst.
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of Month 1 invoice applied immediately on the first billing cycle.
- SLAs: 99.9% platform availability; soft-throttle thresholds and fallback model behavior as documented in the attached appendix.

Attachments included as stubs here for procurement: Suncrest_Amendment_Signature_Stub.pdf and the v2 proposal. I’ve generated the DocuSign envelope for signature — short link below. Once signed we’ll provision the commit in your tenant and enable the burst pocket on 2026-10-01.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign?doc=SUNCREST_AMENDMENT_11392
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/11392

If procurement wants any minor redlines we can accept them as long as they do not change billing mechanics or SLAs; anything material will need an executive approval step.

Thanks again — excited to keep Suncrest scaling with Redwood.

—Marissa
